text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hosni Mubarak had talks yesterday with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and U.S. envoy Dennis Ross on the latest developments in the Israeli-Palestinian talks.

- The council of ministers decided to set up a committee to follow up the project to develop the south of the valley and another committee to develop agricultural and commodity exports. It also decided to set aside 751 million pounds ($220 million) to develop existing airports and build new ones.
- Mubarak had a telephone call from King Hussein of Jordan on Saturday evening on the Israeli-Palestinian talks. Hussein also made a call to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

- An Egyptian delegation left for Kampala yesterday for the first meeting of the commitee of experts of the Nile Basin countries, to discuss setting up a new mechanism for managing and developing the resources of the Nile Basin.
- The cabinet said that Mubarak would make regular inspection visits to the south of the valley to follow implementation of the New Valley project.
- Mubarak will meet writers and intellectuals at the opening of the Cairo International Book Fair next Saturday.
- Turnover on the Egyptian stock exchange last week was 272 million pounds.

- The Council of State ruled that, at Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries, board members who represent public-sector companies were wrong to take shares in Eipico. Now they should either give them back or pay for them at the current market price, it said.
